report.body:
On 1 October 2026, Mossos d’Esquadra officers detained seven men aged 29 to 55
in an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Girona, over their alleged role in a
drug-trafficking organisation. The investigation had identified the
warehouse as serving solely to store and distribute narcotics. Officers
found the seven inside unloading pallets from a trailer to move the hashish into
vans for later distribution. The seven detainees were placed at the
disposal of the Civil and Instruction Section of the Figueres lower court.

Officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish concealed among the trailer's lawful cargo. The drug was packed in large raffia sacks filled with rubber crumb, a
method used to hinder detection at police or customs controls. Police put
the illicit-market value of the seized substance at more than 16.2 million
euros. During the search, officers found a firearm in one of the detainees'
vans. The building was almost entirely open space with nothing indicating
business or residential activity. Investigators kept the case open, without
ruling out further arrests or related actions.

The investigation began in June 2026 after officers in Viladecans intercepted a
van carrying about 2,400 kg of hashish. Officers later determined that the
van's load had come from the industrial warehouse in Cabanes. In early
October, surveillance detected repeated movements of people and vans around the
warehouse and the arrival of an articulated lorry. Officers saw people
swapping the vehicles' original number plates for others fixed with cable ties,
apparently to hinder identification. The trailer was then driven inside the
warehouse and the door was closed. Investigators then moved in with support
from Girona ARRO officers and entered the premises. The seizure was
presented as a large share of the nearly 14,900 kg of hashish the Mossos had
intercepted in 2026 up to 1 October. After the seizure, Catalonia's
interior minister restated her call to raise prison sentences for large-scale
trafficking and to step up action against organised crime.

report.summary: National Police in Palma arrested four men and a woman suspected of belonging to a drug-trafficking group after a months-long investigation. Officers seized 60 kilos of hashish, a 24-kilo parcel plus 36 kilos in a home, alongside cocaine, weapons and about 10,000 euros in cash.
report.body:
Spain's National Police arrested four men and a woman in Palma on suspicion of
belonging to a drug-trafficking group. The investigation was conducted by
Grupo I de Estupefacientes over several months and ended with five arrests,
according to a police statement. Officers learned of a hashish parcel
addressed to a man living in Palma. They intercepted the parcel, which held
24 kilos of hashish, and arrested the recipient on suspicion of drug
trafficking.

In the main suspect's home officers found 36 kilos of hashish, an air rifle with
a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash. A man and a woman were arrested
at that address as the alleged perpetrators of drug trafficking and membership
of a criminal group or organisation. At a second home officers arrested
another suspect who allegedly stored and transported drugs. There officers
found two kilos of cocaine, several doses, cutting substance, a pistol with
nine-millimetre cartridges and a bow with arrows. Officers also found a
hydraulic press allegedly used to compress cocaine.

A fifth person was arrested over links to the case, and police suspect the drugs
were passed to others for smaller-scale sale. The investigation remains
open and further arrests have not been ruled out. Officers from the
Prevention and Reaction Unit, Grupo II de Estupefacientes and the canine guides
unit took part in the searches.

report.title: Man's 4-year term halved to 2 years over 18.6 kg hash smuggling
report.summary: A man in his 40s caught at the Kristiansand ferry terminal with 18.566 kg of hashish had his four-year prison sentence halved on appeal. Agder Court of Appeal sentenced him to two years for the hashish import after finding it unproven that he knew about 996.7 g of cocaine also hidden in the car.
report.body:
A man in his 40s was sentenced to four years in prison after being stopped with
large quantities of drugs at the ferry terminal in Kristiansand. Agder
Court of Appeal later halved the sentence because it was not proved that he knew
about the cocaine he had in the car. Customs officers stopped him at the
ferry terminal in Kristiansand on 6 November last year. He had arrived from
Denmark in a German-registered Mazda belonging to his sister.

Under the boot floor, customs officers found 18.566 kilos of hashish and 996.7
grams of cocaine. The man admitted smuggling the hashish but denied knowing
the car also contained cocaine. Agder District Court sentenced him in
August to four years in prison, and he appealed the sentence and was believed.

He told the court he had borrowed 3,500 euros from a person in Germany and had
been unable to repay it. He said he was pressed to smuggle 15 kilos of
hashish to Norway to clear the debt, plus receive 1,000 euros. He said the
organisers threatened him and his family with violence, once holding a pistol to
his head and breaking his little finger. The Court of Appeal accepts that
he was exposed to serious threats and that his finger was broken. No DNA or
fingerprints from the man were found on the drug packaging. DNA from three
other people was detected, and the court found it unproven that he examined the
drugs after the organisers placed them in the car. The judgment said that
even if he had seen the packages, it would not necessarily have been possible to
tell that one contained cocaine. The court therefore concluded that it was
not proved beyond reasonable doubt that he intended to import the cocaine.

It sentenced him for importing 18.566 kilos of hashish, starting from two years
and ten months and reducing the term for his confession and the threats.
The court noted that he could have contacted the police before crossing the
border and that he stood to gain financially from the smuggling. The final
sentence was two years in prison, halving the District Court's sentence. He
was credited for 374 days already spent in pre-trial detention.

open_questions: The reports give the stop as Tuesday at 2:28 p.m. without a calendar date; 8 September 2026, the Tuesday before the 14 September publications, is used as the approximate incident date.
The 489 pounds was described only as cannabis, with no laboratory confirmation or product breakdown reported.
No value estimate, vehicle description beyond the traffic violations, or allocation of the cannabis between the two men was reported.
No plea or further court outcome beyond the arraignment and custody decisions was reported.
Both accounts attribute the details to the Saratoga County Sheriff's Office and are not independent of that statement.
report.body:
Saratoga County sheriff's deputies stopped a vehicle on the Northway in Clifton
Park at 2:28 p.m. on Tuesday for following too closely and insufficient tail
lamps. The investigation during the stop led to the arrests of 46-year-old
Kevin C. Wilbur of Brushton and 23-year-old Quinton L. Carle of Bombay.
Wilbur and Carle were each charged with criminal possession of cannabis in the
first degree. Wilbur was also cited for following too closely and having
insufficient tail lamps.

Deputies seized 489 pounds (about 221.81 kg) of cannabis in the Northway stop in
Clifton Park. Both men were arraigned before Judge Jennifer Jeram in
Clifton Park Town Court. Wilbur was remanded to the Saratoga County Jail
while Carle was released on his own recognizance pending further proceedings in
that court. Sheriff Jeffrey R. Brown said deputies did excellent police
work and had prevented nearly one-quarter ton of illicit cannabis from reaching
the streets.

The sheriff's office said Wilbur and Carle knowingly and unlawfully possessed
the 489 pounds of cannabis. The case remained pending in Clifton Park Town
Court after the arraignment custody decisions.

report.body:
Kern County deputies arrested 32-year-old Rogelio Lorenzo Francisca from
Guerrero, Mexico, during the Taft cannabis-grow investigation. He was
booked into the Taft jail facility on suspicion of marijuana cultivation,
marijuana for sale, conspiracy and delaying, resisting or obstructing an
officer.

Deputies from the Taft Substation, assisted by the KC-HIDTA task force and the
Taft Police Department, executed a search warrant on October 8, 2026, in the
27000 block of Highway 119 in Taft. During the search, officers eradicated
a total of 660 marijuana plants. Investigators also found dangerous
pesticides within the grow site.

The investigation remains active and ongoing.

cases.why: A change in the law (the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act, signed in May 2024). Law changes go to the Cannabis Freedom Index history, not into the tracker.

attempts.decision_title: South Africa cannabis-use legalisation routed to CFI
attempts.explanation: The Al Jazeera article reports President Cyril Ramaphosa signing the Cannabis for Private Purposes Act, removing cannabis from South Africa's list of outlawed narcotics and allowing adults to grow and consume it, while sale remains illegal except on medical prescription. This is a change to national law, not a raid, seizure, eradication, arrest, prosecution, sentence or other enforcement event. Under the tracker scope, law changes, precedents, landmark cases and national statistics belong in the Cannabis Freedom Index history, not as tracker enforcement reports. No single-operation enforcement figures are given; the 3,000-prisoner figure is a 2022 national total.
